question: Which law prevails in case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a subject in the Concurrent List?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Union law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the case of a conflict between **Union and State laws** on a subject in the **Concurrent List**, the **Union law prevails** as per **Article 254(1) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects where both the Union and State governments can legislate. However, in case of inconsistency, the **Union law** will supersede the State law.
 
• If a State law receives the **President's assent** under **Article 254(2)**, it can prevail over Union law in that particular state. However, Parliament retains the power to override such state laws by making a law on the same subject. *Hence, Union law takes precedence in most cases.*
 
• The primary purpose of giving precedence to Union law is to maintain **uniformity** across the country on matters of national importance.
 
• This principle ensures that there is no conflict in laws affecting citizens across different states and facilitates a cohesive legal framework. *Hence, the correct answer is Union law.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 254 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 254(1)**: When there is a conflict between a law made by the Parliament and a law made by the State Legislature on a subject in the **Concurrent List**, the law made by Parliament shall prevail.
 
• **Article 254(2)**: If a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with an existing Union law, and the State law receives the **President's assent**, the State law can prevail in that particular state. However, the Parliament can override the State law by making another law on the same subject.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three lists in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution. It includes subjects where both the Union and State legislatures can legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include **education, criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, forests, and protection of wildlife**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Union Law Supremacy:**
 
 
• The supremacy of Union law ensures that there is a **uniform legal system** on subjects of national importance, avoiding discrepancies between states.
 
• This principle also ensures that the Union government can address issues of national interest effectively without being constrained by conflicting State laws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Considerations in Article 254:**

 
 
• The **Concurrent List** subjects require careful legislation to avoid conflicts. Parliament has the final authority to ensure uniformity in laws.
 
• The **President's assent** is critical when State laws conflict with Union laws. This provides a constitutional mechanism to resolve conflicts.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Union Law Supremacy:**
 
 
• The Union government enacted the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, which superseded State laws on environmental protection for uniform implementation across India.
 
• In the case of **education policies**, the Union government has consistently framed laws to ensure a standard education system across states, even when State laws differed.
